isaac-g-bryan.text: Authored AB 247 (signed Oct 13, 2025): incarcerated hand-crew firefighters must be paid $7.25 per hour while assigned to an active fire incident, with annual rate review, while keeping existing sentence-credit benefits.

source.title: AB-247 Incarcerated individual hand crew members: wages (leginfo)

isaac-g-bryan.text: Authored ACA 4, a constitutional amendment to repeal the disqualification of people imprisoned for felonies from voting, restoring voting rights to incarcerated citizens (requires two-thirds legislative vote and voter approval).

Authored AB 1388 (chaptered Oct 13, 2025): voids law enforcement settlement agreements that conceal misconduct investigation records and expands public and civilian-oversight access to serious peace officer misconduct records.

Co-authored AB 1537, which bars peace officers from secondary employment arresting, detaining, transporting, or deporting people under federal or out-of-state immigration laws; violations could lead to decertification.

Authored AB 1655, which keeps CalWORKs benefits for families when a child or household member is detained in a federal immigration detention facility, treating the person as temporarily absent from the home.

source.title: AB-1655 CalWORKs: temporary absence: immigration detention (leginfo)

isaac-g-bryan.text: Authored AB 1661: low-production oil wells in the Baldwin Hills must be plugged and abandoned by Dec 31, 2030, with $10,000 monthly penalties funding cash assistance to nearby households with respiratory or reproductive health impacts.

source.title: AB-1661 Oil and gas: low-production wells (leginfo)

isaac-g-bryan.text: Authored AB 1457 requiring cities and counties to conduct outreach, including at least two public workshops, to disadvantaged communities when developing the environmental justice element of their general plans.

source.title: AB-1457 General plan: environmental justice element (leginfo)

isaac-g-bryan.text: Authored AB 1883, prohibiting employers from using AI workplace surveillance tools that recognize emotional states or collect neural data; enforceable by the Labor Commissioner with penalties up to $500 per violation.
Authored AB 1573 (approved Sept 27, 2026), adding victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, and human trafficking to the 'target population' that local housing elements must consider.

source.title: AB-1573 Land use: housing elements: target population (leginfo)

isaac-g-bryan.text: Authored AB 2162 on county housing funding allocations for nonminor dependents and young adults (foster youth); listed as passed.
Co-chaired the Los Angeles County Measure J campaign, which diverts at least 10% of county general funds to community investment and alternatives to incarceration.
Member of the California Legislative Progressive Caucus; elected Vice-Chair of the California Legislative Black Caucus in 2024.

ashley-m-brown.text: Top three priorities: advancing mental health and women's health, strengthening education as a pathway to economic stability, and investing in community-based prevention to create safer communities.

source.title: VOTE411 Voter Guide, State Assembly District 55

ashley-m-brown.text: Supports efforts to address housing shortages but says 'increasing supply alone is not enough'; favors preserving existing affordable housing, expanding homeownership pathways, and protecting against displacement.

source.title: VOTE411 Voter Guide, State Assembly District 55

ashley-m-brown.text: Proposes a whole-child approach to education: expanded school-based mental health services, community schools with wraparound services, and pathways connecting education to economic stability.

source.title: VOTE411 Voter Guide, State Assembly District 55

ashley-m-brown.text: On water: supports long-term sustainability, restricting high-water-use industries, investing in water recycling and infrastructure modernization, with emphasis on protecting low-income communities.

source.title: VOTE411 Voter Guide, State Assembly District 55

ashley-m-brown.text: Per the IJ Action voter guide, Brown "believes that community safety starts with strong schools, accessible mental health care, and sustained investment in youth," listing community safety through prevention and youth investment among her top priorities.
Supports trauma-informed approaches to safety, community-rooted violence prevention, and policies prioritizing mental health, education, and youth opportunity as public safety investments.
Supports equitable education funding, strong labor protections for educators and school staff, and policies that strengthen economic stability for working families.
Supports expanding access to mental health services, strengthening school- and community-based care, protecting women's health, and ensuring preventive support reaches people before crisis.

notes: Bryan's own campaign site could not be fetched (rate-limited); his evidence is his authored bills and Wikipedia/Digital Democracy. He did not answer the VOTE411 questionnaire. Brown has no voting record; no endorsements, tax, guns, transportation, immigration or social-issue positions found for her. Endorsements for Bryan were not verified from a fetched page and are omitted.
